newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai hotel to switch to Chinese management.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai hotel to switch to Chinese management.

text.p: Shanghai's first foreign-managed hotel, the Sheraton Hua Ting, will switch to wholly Chinese management on May 1, marking the end of an era for hotel management in the city, officials said on Friday.
Business is expected to fall off slightly with the change in management, with the hotel no longer having access to bookings made through Sheraton's worldwide network, they said.

When the Sheraton Hua Ting opened for business in 1986, it was the only five-star hotel in Shanghai. Most of the other hotels in the city dated from the pre-1949 era and had hardly been renovated or updated since then.
The ITT Sheraton Corp's management contract for the hotel expires at the end of this month, and will be taken over by the local Shanghai Huating (Group) Corp, which owns the hotel building.
ITT Sheraton's country manager for China, Victor Kimura, said the two sides decided to end the management contract by mutual agreement.
"We have a very good relationship with the Hua Ting Group and we wish them the best," he said by telephone from Beijing.
"For a time, this will definitely affect the source of guests and operating revenue -- there will be a decline," Hua Ting president Gu Yongcai told reporters at a media briefing.
He declined to give figures or forecasts for revenue, but said the occupancy rate of the 1,008 room hotel was 65 percent in the first quarter of 1997, unchanged from the same period in 1996.
Hotel management said the quality of management and service towards guests would continue to be high.
"We have 10 years of management experience," said new general manager Sun Xiuhua. "We believe management and service won't suffer."
Hua Ting currently owns and manages eight hotels in Shanghai and manages three others on behalf of other companies.
ITT Sheraton is now considering other hotel opportunities in Shanghai, including both management and investment, Kimura said.
"We view Shanghai as critically important -- both Shanghai and Pudong," he said.
China is promoting Shanghai's Pudong area as the country's premier financial and industrial zone.
